AdaptersSettings.description:
``[adapters]`` — the operator's directory of adapter artifacts and their manifests.

Opt-in, per application (ADR-0061 rule 2): **empty means the whole feature is off**, and a
deployment that has never heard of adapters is unaffected by every part of it.

directory.description: Directory holding adapter artifacts and their reviewed manifests. Empty — the default — turns adapters off entirely; nothing is scanned, registered or routed.
directory.title: Directory

AdaptersSettings.title: AdaptersSettings

ConsoleSettings.description:
Where WeightRoomGym is, when one fronts this application (row WM2).

Set, the top bar gains the suite's tab strip: WeightRoomGym itself and the peer applications
through it (``<url>/apps/<name>``). Unset — the default — nothing is rendered: an
application knows only its own port, and a strip of loopback links another machine cannot
reach would be a strip of dead links.

url.description: WeightRoomGym's base URL (https://<host>:8769); empty renders no application tab strip.
url.title: Url

ConsoleSettings.title: ConsoleSettings

EvidenceSettings.description: ``[evidence]`` — the optional FreeWeight evidence source (Phase 6, ADR-0026).

accept_schema_majors.description: Which `benchmark.evidence_bundle` schema majors this installation reads. May only narrow what this build carries payload models for, never widen it.
accept_schema_majors.title: Accept Schema Majors

allowed_source_hosts.description: Fetch allowlist for evidence import URLs (ADR-0026 §3).
allowed_source_hosts.title: Allowed Source Hosts

freeweight_api_key_env.description: Environment variable naming a bearer token, or empty (ADR-0026).
freeweight_api_key_env.title: Freeweight Api Key Env

freeweight_api_key_file.description: Path to a file containing a bearer token, or empty (ADR-0026).
freeweight_api_key_file.title: Freeweight Api Key File

freeweight_url.description: Empty means not configured, not unavailable.
freeweight_url.title: Freeweight Url

EvidenceSettings.title: EvidenceSettings

ExecutionSettings.description: ``[execution]`` — concurrency, timeout and retry policy for job execution (Phase 4-5).

max_attempts.description: Attempts before a job is marked failed.
max_attempts.title: Max Attempts

max_concurrent_jobs.description: Raise only on multi-GPU or CPU-only setups.
max_concurrent_jobs.title: Max Concurrent Jobs

ExecutionSettings.title: ExecutionSettings

FakeProviderSettings.description:
``[provider.fake]`` — override the declared model ``kind = "fake"`` serves (E6).

Every field defaults to ``None``, in which case :func:`loadcoach.infrastructure.providers.
factory.build_provider` uses its own small built-in fake model — one whose VRAM estimate never
trips the ``insufficient_vram`` hard constraint (routing.md §4), so a fake-provider journey is
reproducible on any machine rather than gated on a free GPU.

Setting these lets an operator deliberately reproduce ``insufficient_vram`` end to end, with
the whole ``estimate`` block populated, on a machine with plenty of free VRAM. All four fields
must be set together, or none: the estimate's KV term (``2 × layers × kv_heads × head_dim × 2
bytes`` for the assumed f16 precision, multiplied by the served context) dominates
``size_bytes`` at any interesting context length, so ``size_bytes`` alone cannot reliably
provoke the rejection this block exists to reach.

head_dim.description: Per-head dimension to declare, overriding the small built-in default.
head_dim.title: Head Dim

kv_heads.description: Key/value head count to declare, overriding the small built-in default.
kv_heads.title: Kv Heads

layers.description: Transformer block count to declare, overriding the small built-in default.
layers.title: Layers

size_bytes.description: On-disk weight size to declare, overriding the small built-in default.
size_bytes.title: Size Bytes

FakeProviderSettings.title: FakeProviderSettings

format.description: text, json, or auto (text on a TTY, json otherwise).
format.title: Format

include_content.description: Log full prompts and responses. Off by default: only hashes and lengths are logged.
include_content.title: Include Content

ProviderRegistrationSettings.description:
One ``[providers.<name>]`` block: a provider LoadCoach registers, by name and kind.

LC-E1, generalized (ADR-0055). The name is the operator's, and it is what explanations, the
models UI and ``doctor`` refer to; the kind decides which adapter is constructed.

base_url.description: The provider's API endpoint, where its kind takes one.
base_url.title: Base Url

enabled.description: Whether this registration is registered at all. A disabled registration keeps its block in the file — nothing about it is lost or has to be retyped — and is skipped by the registry: no handle is built for it, discovery never lists it, routing cannot reach it, and the models it last served answer `unavailable_reason = 'provider_disabled'`. Disabling every registration is refused: an application with no provider registers nothing and serves nothing.
enabled.title: Enabled

kind.description: Which provider adapter serves this registration.
kind.title: Kind

memory_high_bytes.description: For kind='llamacpp': the throttle point below memory_max_bytes (MemoryHigh). Requires memory_max_bytes and must be below it.
memory_high_bytes.title: Memory High Bytes

memory_max_bytes.description: For kind='llamacpp': a host-memory cap on every server this registration launches (ADR-0119) — a systemd-run user scope with MemoryMax at this value and swap denied, so a server that does not fit is killed rather than swapping the host. Unset launches uncapped.
memory_max_bytes.title: Memory Max Bytes

model_directory.description: For kind='llamacpp': the directory of GGUF weights this server serves. Required for that kind, meaningless for every other — a llama.cpp registration launches and supervises its own server rather than talking to one that is already running.
model_directory.title: Model Directory

remote.description: Whether this registration is somewhere other than this machine. Declared, never inferred from the kind or the URL: an OpenAI-compatible endpoint on loopback is local, and the same kind pointed at a hosted API is remote (ADR-0055 rule 4).
remote.title: Remote

server_path.description: For kind='llamacpp': the server binary, found on PATH by default.
server_path.title: Server Path

state_dir.description: For kind='llamacpp': where the supervisor keeps its per-server state and the artifact-digest file (ADR-0071). Empty uses `<data_dir>/llamacpp/<name>`.
state_dir.title: State Dir

ProviderRegistrationSettings.title: ProviderRegistrationSettings

ProviderSettings.description: The default model provider LoadCoach talks to.

fake.description: Override the model kind='fake' declares, to provoke insufficient_vram on purpose (E6); absent by default, and absent entirely on a normal install. See spec.md §12.

kind.description: Which provider serves the models: ollama, or fake for tests.
kind.title: Kind

ProviderSettings.title: ProviderSettings

ProvidersSettings.description:
Cross-provider policy, plus the ``[providers.<name>]`` registrations themselves.

``allow_remote`` is policy — may *any* remote provider be routed to at all — and it is
evaluated above a registration's own ``remote`` flag: a remote registration in a deployment
that disallows remote is configured, visible and never routed to (ADR-0077 rule 4).

Every other key under ``[providers]`` is a registration, so this model allows extras and
validates them itself rather than forbidding them: ``[providers.local]`` and
``[providers] allow_remote`` share one TOML table, and pydantic sees both in one mapping.

allow_remote.description: Permit a remote provider at all — an explicit, deliberate opt-in.
allow_remote.title: Allow Remote

registrations.description: The named registrations, keyed by their operator-chosen names.
registrations.title: Registrations

ProvidersSettings.title: ProvidersSettings

QueueSettings.description: ``[queue]`` — job queue depth, leasing and ageing policy (Phase 5).

cancelling_watchdog_seconds.description: How long a job may sit in `cancelling` before the scheduler forces it to `cancelled` and records that it did (queue §8, §9).
cancelling_watchdog_seconds.title: Cancelling Watchdog Seconds

idempotency_ttl_hours.description: How long a job's idempotency key stays reserved after enqueue. A key reused after this starts new work rather than replaying an old result (api.md §4, data model §2).
idempotency_ttl_hours.title: Idempotency Ttl Hours

lease_renewal_interval_seconds.description: lease_seconds must exceed 3x this plus slack.
lease_renewal_interval_seconds.title: Lease Renewal Interval Seconds

max_active_per_source.description: Active (non-terminal) jobs one source — a token, or an X-Client-Name on loopback — may hold at once; a submission past it is refused with QUEUE_FULL naming the source and the cap (spec §14). 0 disables the per-source cap.
max_active_per_source.title: Max Active Per Source

QueueSettings.title: QueueSettings

ResidencySettings.description: ``[residency]`` — model unload policy, per device (Phase 5, queue §6).
ResidencySettings.title: ResidencySettings

base_switch_penalty.description: Two-level residency's penalty for a candidate that would need its own base loaded while another base is resident (routing §6.1, ADR-0066). Chosen, not measured: twice prefer_resident_bonus, so a base switch is never decided by the tie-break the bonus exists to be. A deployment that has measured its own load times should set it from them.
base_switch_penalty.title: Base Switch Penalty

remote_cost_factor.description: The cost factor applied to a remote provider's candidates (routing §6). 1.0 is always used for local providers; anything below 1 prefers local at equal capability.
remote_cost_factor.title: Remote Cost Factor

require_adapter_evidence.description: Refuse to *route* to an adapter subject with no measured evidence for the profile's top-weighted capability (ADR-0064 rule 3). On by default: until FreeWeight measures adapters, every adapter subject is unmeasured, so adapters are invisible to routed selection while pins keep working. That is 'no benchmark, no use' behaving correctly.
require_adapter_evidence.title: Require Adapter Evidence

task_profiles_path.description: A task_profiles.toml to import at startup instead of the shipped one. Empty means the shipped file. The import is an upsert per (profile_id, version), so a file naming a shipped profile replaces it and one naming a new id adds it.
task_profiles_path.title: Task Profiles Path

RuntimeModelOverride.description:
A per-model override of the default runtime profile (ADR-0023).

Every field left ``None`` says nothing and lets the ``[runtime]`` default through.
``kv_cache_precision`` and ``flash_attention`` are llama.cpp launch settings (ADR-0120): a
resolved profile that sets either for an Ollama registration is rejected by name at routing
time, and a quantized cache without flash attention likewise — both are evaluated on the
*resolved* profile, because the default level may supply the other half.

context_size.description: Context window to serve for this specific model, in tokens.
context_size.title: Context Size

flash_attention.description: Flash attention for this model (llamacpp only, ADR-0120).
flash_attention.title: Flash Attention

kv_cache_precision.description: KV-cache precision for this model: f16, q8_0 or q4_0 (llamacpp only, ADR-0120). q8_0 and q4_0 require flash attention on the resolved profile.
kv_cache_precision.title: Kv Cache Precision

RuntimeModelOverride.title: RuntimeModelOverride

RuntimeSettings.description:
``[runtime]`` — the default runtime profile every execution resolves against (ADR-0023).

Every field defaults to a value meaning "provider decides"; ``context_size = 0`` and
``kv_cache_precision = ""`` are that sentinel in TOML's type system, since the profile itself
(``baseaicore.RuntimeProfile``) uses ``None`` for the same meaning once loaded.

context_size.description: Context window to serve, in tokens. 0 leaves it to the provider; a task profile with min_context_tokens sets it explicitly where the provider reports context_configurable.
context_size.title: Context Size

flash_attention.description: Empty/false leaves it to the provider.
flash_attention.title: Flash Attention

keep_alive.description: How long the provider holds a model resident after a call.
keep_alive.title: Keep Alive

kv_cache_precision.description: Empty leaves it to the provider. f16, q8_0 or q4_0 is sent to llama.cpp launches; q8_0 and q4_0 require flash_attention = true (ADR-0120).
kv_cache_precision.title: Kv Cache Precision

models.description: Per-model runtime overrides, keyed by canonical model ID.
models.title: Models

RuntimeSettings.title: RuntimeSettings

allow_lan_exposure.description: Acknowledges a deliberate bind to every interface (0.0.0.0). Without it such a bind refuses to start.
allow_lan_exposure.title: Allow Lan Exposure

allowed_hosts.description: Host header values accepted on a non-loopback bind, against DNS rebinding. Comma-separated in the environment.
allowed_hosts.title: Allowed Hosts

failed_auth_per_minute.description: Failed authentications one address may make per minute before it is refused with 429 for the rest of the minute (ADR-0014 §6). 0 disables.
failed_auth_per_minute.title: Failed Auth Per Minute

host.description: Interface to bind. Loopback by default; anything else requires allowed_hosts and at least one active API token (ADR-0026).
host.title: Host

max_body_bytes.description: The largest request body accepted, refused with 413 before buffering (Security Standards §14). Matches SetSpec's envelope limit, the largest document any endpoint parses.
max_body_bytes.title: Max Body Bytes

port.description: TCP port for the web UI and the API.
port.title: Port

rate_limit_burst.description: How many requests one credential may make at once before the rate applies.
rate_limit_burst.title: Rate Limit Burst

rate_limit_per_minute.description: Requests per minute one credential may make to /api/v1, sustained (spec §14). A token bucket: rate_limit_burst may arrive at once, then this rate. 0 disables. At the limit a caller gets 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After, never a dropped request.
rate_limit_per_minute.title: Rate Limit Per Minute

trusted_proxies.description: CIDR networks of reverse proxies whose X-Forwarded-For may be believed (ADR-0014 §7). When the connecting peer is inside one, the client address — what the failed-authentication brake and the unauthenticated rate bucket key on — is taken from the last untrusted hop of X-Forwarded-For; from any other peer the header is ignored entirely, because anyone can send it. Empty by default: behind a proxy with this unset, every caller shares the proxy's address and one caller's failures brake them all. Comma-separated in the environment.
trusted_proxies.title: Trusted Proxies

auto_migrate.description: Migrate on startup. Unset means true on SQLite and false on PostgreSQL, where a failed migration cannot be rolled back automatically (database standards §5.1).
auto_migrate.title: Auto Migrate

backup_retention.description: Automatic pre-migration backups kept before the oldest is rotated away.
backup_retention.title: Backup Retention

content_retention_hours.description: How long a finished job keeps its prompt and response text before the retention sweep replaces them with their hashes (spec §14: content is stored as hashes by default; data model §3). 0 scrubs at the first sweep after completion. A queued job always keeps its transcript until it has run. Runtime-changeable.
content_retention_hours.title: Content Retention Hours

database_url.description: SQLAlchemy URL. Unset resolves to a SQLite file under the XDG data directory; PostgreSQL is the other supported dialect (ADR-0006).
database_url.title: Database Url

retain_content.description: Keep prompt and response text for ever, disabling the retention sweep. A privacy decision, so config-only: it cannot be changed through PUT /settings.
retain_content.title: Retain Content

statement_timeout_ms.description: PostgreSQL statement (and lock) timeout. Unset leaves the server default; SQLite uses its own busy timeout, which the engine always sets.
statement_timeout_ms.title: Statement Timeout Ms

json_schema.description:
The complete, validated LoadCoach configuration.

Constructed only by :func:`load_settings`, which resolves the precedence chain first — never
call ``Settings(**raw_dict)`` directly on unmerged input, or the file/env/CLI layering in
configuration standards §1 is bypassed.
json_schema.title: Settings

runtime_changeable.description: Finish in-flight work and claim nothing new.
The measured-weight floor below which a decision is flagged low_evidence.
Evidence below this confidence is ignored (routing §5).
The cost factor applied to a remote provider's candidates (routing §6).
Hours a finished job keeps its prompt and response text (spec §14).
